issues.description: Specification of `delimiter` conflates symbolic constants with literal characters in the same namespace.
issues.detail: The dictionary `_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS` mixes two disjoint sorts — single-character delimiters and OpenAPI style names — under one key space. The precondition `delimiter in _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS` is therefore not expressible as one clean predicate. A `Literal[',', '|', ' ', 'pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited']` type or two parameters would let the reader state the precondition without enumerating folklore.

issues.description: Frame condition on the multi-value branch is undocumented and silently ignored.
issues.detail: When the same parameter appears multiple times, `items` is already a list and the delimiter argument is silently discarded. The docstring mentions this in a Note, but the postcondition the caller actually gets — "split iff scalar, else as-is" — is not stated as a contract. Callers requesting `delimiter=' '` on `?x=a b&x=c d` will get `['a b','c d']`, which is plausible but unreasoned.

issues.description: `ValueError` from inside the request handler is a smuggled goto across the HTTP boundary.
issues.detail: Per the existing docstring, `get_param_as_*` raises `HTTPBadRequest` for malformed client input and `ValueError` only from transform callbacks. Raising a bare `ValueError` for a programmer-supplied bad delimiter mixes two distinct failure modes onto the same channel. A `TypeError` or a precondition assertion at call time would separate "client sent garbage" from "developer passed a nonsense argument."

issues.description: Identity entries `',': ','`, `'|': '|'`, `' ': ' '` are redundant and obscure intent.
issues.detail: Half of `_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS` maps a character to itself. The map exists only to translate two symbolic names. Splitting it into `{'pipeDelimited': '|', 'spaceDelimited': ' '}` plus an allowlist `{',', '|', ' '}` would make the precondition expressible in one line and the table self-explanatory. Elegance is not optional; this is a small failure of it.

issues.description: Tests demonstrate behavior on examples but do not establish the invariant.
issues.detail: The added tests confirm the four happy paths and one rejection. None of them probe the boundary cases that would distinguish "reasoned" from "tested": empty string value, single token with no delimiter, trailing delimiter, `keep_blank_qs_values=True` interaction, or `default` returned when missing. Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence; the spec here remains demonstrated rather than proved.

review.summary: The feature is small, localized, and the control flow is structured — there is no smuggled goto in the implementation itself. The defect is at the specification layer: the `delimiter` argument's domain is a hybrid of literal characters and OpenAPI style names sharing one key space, which makes the precondition awkward to state and the lookup table half-redundant. Error signaling raises `ValueError` for a developer mistake on the same channel reserved for malformed client input, conflating two distinct failure modes. The tests demonstrate the documented examples but do not exercise boundary cases (empty values, blank-keeping, missing param with `default`, trailing delimiters), so correctness rests on inspection of three lines rather than on a stated invariant. REASONED-ENOUGH-TO-LAND with the noted cleanups; not REFUSED.
